profile.regional_context: Located on the University of Texas J.J. Pickle Research Campus (Austin, TX)

reading.body:
The Cortex supercomputer sits on the University of Texas J.J. Pickle Research Campus in Austin, but the operator's published specifications do not include power capacity, square footage, or IT load figures. Wikipedia names other TACC systems including Stampede, Lonestar, and Maverick, but does not mention Cortex by name in accessible content. Without published power consumption or density data, the campus's capacity cannot be estimated.

Texas publishes power figures for only 18 of its 133 mapped data center facilities, totaling 468 MW across the state. This campus does not appear in the published capacity ranking, meaning either its power draw is below the 19th-ranked facility in the state, or it has not disclosed the figure. The state context provides no grid constraints or available capacity data.

No certifications qualifying this campus for AI workloads are published. Without specifications on power, cooling, networking, or tenant commitments, this facility cannot be assessed against the thesis that compute availability drives AI scaling.
